text: I have a proclamation here to read. Since 1973, the National Trust of Canada has designated the third Monday in February of each year as National Heritage Day. speaker: Other
text: And agenda item 5.2 is a proclamation with respect to World Lymphedema Day.

speaker: provenzano
text: Whereas lymphedema is an incurable disease effect afflicting more than 300 million people worldwide with disfigurement, disabilities, discomfort, pain and distress. Whereas approximately 1 million Canadians are living and suffering with lymphedema, whether primary inherited, present at birth or manifesting itself later in life from genetic defects or secondary developed from bodily traumas such as cancer treatment, radiation therapy, major surgery, severe burns or other injuries. Whereas lymphedema is an accumulation of high protein lymphatic fluid that causes swelling which impairs mobility function, causes pain that significantly impacts quality of life and can lead to severe infection and can lead to loss of use of limbs for the affected person regardless of age or gender. Whereas there's currently no cure from lymphedema. Recognition of the severe physical, emotional, psychosocial and financial impacts and consequences of lymphedema. There's time to support the greatest individuals living with this disability disease as well as their caregivers and families. And 2022 marks the seventh annual year where World Lymphedema Day is observed and recognized throughout Canada and the world to increase public attention, awareness and action related to this serious, chronic and progressive disease. And therefore I, Christian Provenzano as Mayor of the City of Sault Ste. Marie do hereby proclaim March 6th, 2022 as World Lymphedema Day in the City of Sault Ste. Marie.

speaker: Other
text: Under agenda item 5.3, anti-human trafficking awareness day.

speaker: provenzano
text: Whereas human trafficking is defined as recruiting, transporting, transferring, receiving, holding, concealing or harboring a person or exercising controlled direction of influence over the movements of a person to exploit them or to assist in facilitating their exploitation. Whereas in February 22nd, 2007, Canadian House of Commons passed a motion condemning the trafficking of women and children across international borders for the purposes of sexual exploitation. The House of Commons proclaimed February 22nd as human trafficking awareness day to help bring awareness to the magnitude of modern day slavery in Canada and abroad and encourage Canadians to take steps to combat human trafficking. Whereas Hope Alliance is a provincially recognized anti-human trafficking coalition consisting of 30 plus agencies within the Algoma region. Agency sectors include criminal justice, social services, the medical sector. Whereas recruitment begins as young as age 11 years old. 90% sex trafficking occurs in Canada. 97% of human trafficking survivors are women and girls. Whereas individuals are more at risk due to COVID-19 to the virtual platform and spending more time on online websites and apps including Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, and Tinder as means to recruit individuals and many who are requiring services and finding more services online and in person through agencies such as, but not limited to, Algoma Family Services, Social Service Administration Board, John Howard Society, Sault Ste. Marie, Canadian Mental Health Association, Victim Services of Algoma, and the Canadian Human Trafficking Hotline. Whereas learning to recognize early warning signs of human trafficking and where to obtain necessary assistance and treatment gives families better opportunities to lead productive lives. And therefore I, Christian Providence Analyst, Mayor of the City of Sault Ste. Marie, do hereby proclaim February 22nd as Human Trafficking Awareness Day. We acknowledge Hope Alliance for their efforts in bringing attention to this important day and we encourage all citizens of Sault Ste. Marie to work together and raise awareness of human trafficking in our community.

text: Agenda item 5.4 is a proclamation regarding Pink Shirt Day.

speaker: provenzano
text: Whereas Pink Shirt Day began as an act of kindness in 2007 when two students wore pink shirts to school after witnessing a younger student being bullied for wearing one. Whereas Pink Shirt Day has evolved into a global call to action against bullying and discrimination in creating safe spaces for everyone in our schools, workplaces, and communities. Whereas we all share our collective responsibility to ensure that acts of bullying, discrimination, harassment, intimidation, and violence are unacceptable as these could have a profound effect on an individual's sense of safety, self-worth, and ability to learn. Whereas Pink Shirt Day is an opportunity for each of us to stand up against injustice and collectively declare intolerance against all forms of bullying, recognizing our efforts to build a community that fosters respect, inclusion, fairness, equity, and compassion. Whereas Pink Shirt Day is an opportunity to actively promote and encourage respect, empathy, compassion, and kind behavior towards one another. And therefore, I, Christian Provenzanos, mayor of the City of Sault Ste. Marie, hereby proclaim Wednesday, February 23rd, 2022 as Pink Shirt Day in the City of Sault Ste. Marie. Before we move on, Madam Clerk, to 5.5, just in the spirit of Pink Shirt Day, I just want to recognize that a lot of people are really struggling right now due to a number of factors, a main one, which is the pandemic and the effect that it's had on all of us socially and emotionally. A lot of people have made a lot of sacrifices. A lot of people haven't been able to see people for the last couple of years that they would have liked to spend more time with. And a lot of people have made significant adjustments in their own lives to accommodate and act in accord with the larger public health recommendations. And you can see and feel how people are tired and I think impatient, and frankly, really hoping that our lives get back to normal. And we're hopeful that that will, it can happen soon, recognizing that we still have to all be respectful of public health advice, and that we all can see that the current strain of COVID is certainly a very, a virulent and contagious one. I think I'd ask them in the context of this, in the spirit of Pink Shirt Day, that we all dig deep and try and find as much patience as we can for each other and as much kindness as we can for each other. Because my sense of things is that a lot of people are having a difficult time. And that manifests itself and shows up in different ways. But it's, if you can be anything, you can be kind. And I think it'll go a long way in our community if we continue to support each other and help each other. I wanna encourage everybody to do that as best they can. Madam Clerk, we can move on to 5.5.

speaker: rickvanstaveren
text: Good afternoon. Give you an update on economic development encompassing last year and some of the plans going into this year. On the first quarter of 2020, the transition of the economic development staff from the Sault Ste. Marie Economic Development Corporation to the City of Sault Ste. Marie began. The process entailed moving all staff processes, functions, such as finance and operations to direct line reporting into the community development and enterprise services service area. In 2021, the city recruited a number of staff positions, including a Director of Economic Development, a Manager of Business Development and a Manager of Business Attraction. Team is broken down into three components, business attraction, which is focused on bringing businesses to the City of Sault Ste. Marie, business retention and expansion, which is focused on supporting and growing existing businesses in Sault Ste. Marie and small business and entrepreneurship, which supports the development and growth of entrepreneurs and small business in Sault Ste. Marie. The year of 2021 was a building year for the economic development team from the onboarding process, the implementation of CRM and sales funnel practices, introduction to the Sault Ste. Marie business community and ongoing client support, including accessing COVID-19 business supports. In the attached presentation, you're going to find a complete set of metrics that touch all aspects of economic development. We also developed an economic development impact calculator based upon recognized best practices in the economic development field. Calculator looks at overall impact that job creation has on our local economy using StatsCan data, as well as impact multipliers and local salary information to calculate the total financial impact on our economy. Key achievements for 2021 for business retention and expansion included over 150 direct engagements with stakeholders and local businesses, completion of a virtual funding forum that had 70 plus participants and generated five potential funding opportunities, completion of a small business survey that had over 100 participants that generated 53 follow-up calls that were completing in Q1-22, and funding requests in process have the potential to add 20 plus jobs. Business attraction successes included follow-up of over 50 leads sourced through cold calling, referrals or inbound calls. These calls have led to advanced conversations with four companies with the potential to generate over 700 jobs. Staff also engaged with 18 leads generated through a contracted lead generation firm, Return on Investment, which has identified three potential opportunities which could lead to an additional 100 jobs. We continue to focus on our five key strategic industries, advanced manufacturing, lottery and gaming, smart energy clean tech, digital economy, and aviation aerospace. We've modified the list based upon opportunities that have been identified now to include green hydrogen, green energy, and biomass processing. The Small Business and Entrepreneurship Center handled over 511 direct inquiries in 2021. In addition, they conducted over 100 client consultations, helped start four new business, and hosted 14 workshops with combined attendance of 200. The Startup Company Plus and Summer Company Program had ongoing success as they have had in the past. Other notable events were the Bridges to Better Business, pitch competition that generated a virtual audience of 130 participants and raised over $17,000 in cash and in-kind contributions to provide pricing for the winners. A three extension was also negotiated to the lease of the Canal District site, which is where the Millworks Center for Entrepreneurship is domiciled. A review was conducted of initiatives either initiated or proposed by the previous Economic Development Corporation staff to assist in our go-forward strategy. These included, but were not limited, to web development, social media usage and strategy, downtown revitalization, Port of Algoma, industrial land usage and pricing, Millworks operations, business retention and expansion program, business acquisition program, sales lead generation RFP, and future marketing plans. From this review, we've built our go-forward strategy for 2022, incorporating best practices as well as new ideas. Supplementing the execution of best practices, the team is involved with several opportunities, including implementation of the Foreign Trade Zone Program, the Canada Water Agency bid, and multiple funding support efforts for local businesses. We continue to work closely with NOHFC and FedNor to provide support to the business community. Staff has assembled a skilled and motivated team to advance economic development in Sault Ste. Marie. We've implemented a core toolkit and put in place processes that continue to be enhanced, such as web, social media, CRM, metrics, et cetera. And a number of positive indicators for the community point to future growth opportunities. These would be in our sales pipeline, industrial and commercial building permits, inbound information requests, and industry-focused strategy execution, et cetera. So the team looks forward to advancing economic development in Sault Ste. Marie and to providing regular updates and metrics to city council moving forward. Thank you.
